clue.text: Hector's hint about 1 Down for starters

definitions.note: read as 'Hector is': to hector someone is to bully them, so the verb is defined with 's as a joining 'is'

indicators.note: about means the hint goes around the starters, enclosing them

parts.note: to intimate is to hint at something
the starting letters of '1 Down', reading the 1 as I

explanation.surface: Someone called Hector drops a hint about an earlier crossword clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1 of '1 Down' is read as the letter I, so its starters are I and D. 'Hector's' is read as 'Hector is', the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To hector is to bully or browbeat someone, which is a synonym for frightening them into compliance.

clue.text: Dope from UK province to the north

definitions.note: slang for information or inside knowledge

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means the letters are read upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: of can mean from, as in 'of noble birth'
NI is Northern Ireland, the UK province

explanation.surface: Drugs being smuggled down from Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the north' turns OF + NI (OFNI) upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope in slang means gen or information, which shortens to the informal word.

clue.text: Son leaving highlights in hair

indicators.note: the son is going away, so his letter departs from the word for highlights

parts.note: to highlight something is to stress it, so highlights gives the verb form

explanation.surface: A boy walks out of the salon while his hair is being coloured with highlights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' removes one S (son) from STRESSES.
explanation.definitionFit: Tresses are long locks of a person's hair, a literary synonym.

clue.text: Activity for fresher in tutorial, with Mac crashing

indicators.note: a computer crashing goes haywire, signalling that these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A first-year student's Apple laptop crashes during a tutorial.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of IN, TUTORIAL and MAC together are rearranged; 'with' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Matriculation is formal enrolment at a university, an event every new first-year undergraduate goes through.

clue.text: Darned entertaining school games possibly rained on

indicators.note: entertaining guests means holding them within, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: darned is a mild euphemism for damned
PE, physical education, is a school subject that may include games

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the rain spoiled the school sports day.
explanation.walkthrough: Darned is a polite stand-in for damned; PE is physical education, the school subject that includes games.
explanation.definitionFit: Dampened means made wet, as happens to anything caught in a shower.

clue.text: Something fisherman uses, turning on taps for fish

indicators.note: turning round means the word for the fisherman's tool is read backwards

parts.note: an angler or trawlerman uses a net
C and H mark the cold and hot taps

explanation.surface: An angler's kit item and turning on the taps, then a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above; C and H are the cold and hot tap markings.
explanation.definitionFit: The tench is a freshwater species of the carp family, an example of the category.

clue.text: A few wanting nothing with duck

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the nothing is removed

parts.note: a few means some
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A few people left with nothing but a duck to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' takes the O (nothing) from SOME, leaving SME, then W is added.
explanation.definitionFit: The smew is a small diving bird of the sawbill family, an example of a waterfowl species.

clue.text: Irate about work, that chap's one suffering a shock

indicators.note: about means going around, so the angry word surrounds the others

parts.note: irate means mad, angry
OP is short for opus, a work
he refers to that chap

explanation.surface: An angry man is suffering from shock over his work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' is misdirection: it is a shock of hair, not a fright.
explanation.definitionFit: A shock is a thick bushy mass of hair, so a person with a tousled mop of it fits.

clue.text: The two of us are going to jump in a fountain

parts.words: The two of us are going to
parts.note: we'll is the contraction of 'we will', i.e. the two of us are going to
spring means jump

explanation.surface: A couple plan to leap into a public fountain together.
explanation.definitionFit: A wellspring is a natural source of water, a spring or fount from which it flows.

clue.text: Escape introduction to Taylor Swift

parts.note: to flee is to escape

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: An escape route into the world of pop star Taylor Swift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swift' looks like part of the singer's name, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleet as an adjective means fast or nimble, a literary synonym for quick.

clue.text: Clip with Man U playing, inspiring one of City

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so the letter is drawn inside
playing about suggests the letters move around into another order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A football clip of Manchester United playing, featuring a Manchester City player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges CLIP + MANU to MUNCIPAL; 'inspiring' then takes in I (one).
explanation.definitionFit: Municipal describes things belonging to a town or urban local authority, so it means pertaining to a city.

clue.text: Ring with awfully garish tip for person with beautiful hand

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them

indicators.note: awfully suggests these letters are badly arranged and must be reordered

explanation.surface: Phoning someone with a terribly loud tip for a beautician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand' means handwriting, not the part of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: A calligraphist practises decorative penmanship, and a fine hand is good handwriting.

clue.text: German writer's penning long, scary tales

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as in a pen, so the writer's name holds the other word

parts.note: Friedrich Schiller was a German poet and playwright
to long for is to pine

explanation.surface: A German author writing long, frightening stories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penning' looks like writing but means enclosing; the long word goes in just after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Spine-chillers are horror stories or films that frighten the audience, so they are frightening narratives.

clue.text: Dealing with e.g. vinaigrette Sally chucked out

indicators.note: chucked out means thrown away, so the short name is removed from the longer phrase

parts.note: vinaigrette is an example of a salad dressing
Sal is a short form of the name Sally

explanation.surface: Someone handling the fact that Sally threw away the vinaigrette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' is a name here, shortened to its familiar form, not a sortie or a witty remark.
explanation.definitionFit: To address a problem is to tackle or attend to it, so addressing it means handling it.

clue.text: Controversial part of PhD is put edifyingly

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A doctoral thesis presented in an instructive way turns out to be contentious.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disputed is argued over or contested, hence a matter of disagreement.

clue.text: Embarrassed-looking nincompoop back in dating app

indicators.note: back means the words are read in reverse order and direction

parts.note: an embarrassed face goes red
a nit is a fool

explanation.surface: A blushing fool found on a dating app.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses RED + NIT. A nit is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinder is a well-known smartphone matchmaking service, an example of the category.

clue.text: Country singer with simple material

parts.note: Johnny Cash was a country singer
mere means simple or nothing more than

explanation.surface: A country music star dressed in plain fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashmere is fine wool from Kashmir goats, used as a fabric for clothing.

clue.text: Engineers twice getting a low grade study again

indicators.note: twice says the engineers' abbreviation is written a second time in a row

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
D is a low exam grade

explanation.surface: A pair of engineers getting a poor mark and studying again.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (Royal Engineers) appears twice, then A and D.
explanation.definitionFit: To reread a text is to go over it a second time, perusing it once more.

clue.text: Opposes further exams plugged by head of school

indicators.note: plugged means stopped up from inside, so the head letter goes into the exams

parts.note: resits are exams taken again after failure

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A head teacher opposes more exams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plugged by' puts S (first letter of school) inside RESITS. Resits are British exam retakes.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist is to oppose or withstand something.

clue.text: Maybe Ford's vice-president, working

parts.note: Kamala Harris was US vice-president
on means working or functioning

explanation.surface: A car company boss and its vice-president at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ford' suggests the carmaker but is the actor Harrison Ford, so 'Maybe' marks an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Harrison is the forename of actor Ford, an example of a person bearing it.

clue.text: More seasoned sailor, I heard, in odd places

parts.note: an old salt is an experienced sailor

indicators.note: taking the odd places means the first, third and fifth letters only

explanation.surface: An experienced seaman's report of what he heard in strange ports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I heard' looks like a sound signal but is the source of letters: take its 1st, 3rd and 5th.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltier means having more salt, so food made saltier is more seasoned.

clue.text: Job for Renaissance artist? He's working with Plasticine

indicators.note: working here means kneaded and reshaped, so the letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A Renaissance painter is modelling with children's clay.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of HE'S and PLASTICINE are reworked; Plasticine is a British brand of modelling clay.
explanation.definitionFit: Michelangelo painted the ceiling of this Vatican chapel, a famous commission for the Renaissance master.

clue.text: Upset, cancel court claim

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to axe a project is to cancel it

explanation.surface: A disappointed litigant cancels a lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'claim' is a verb here, meaning to demand as due.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact payment is to demand or insist on it, a synonym of the verb meaning to require.

clue.text: Begs lady to undress? How shocking!

indicators.note: undressing strips the outer letters off each word, leaving the middle

explanation.surface: A man implores a woman to strip, and someone is scandalised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to undress' strips BEGS to EG and LADY to AD.
explanation.definitionFit: Egad is an old-fashioned oath expressing surprise, an exclamation like 'goodness me'.

clue.text: Suggest annuities should be redistributed

indicators.note: redistributed means shared out again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A financial adviser hints that pension investments ought to be shared out differently.
explanation.definitionFit: To insinuate is to hint or imply something indirectly, often unpleasantly.

clue.text: Decorating attic in grubby clothes

indicators.note: clothes here is a verb: the outer words dress and cover the answer

parts.note: the letters run from the end of attic through in to the start of grubby

explanation.surface: Someone decorates the loft wearing dirty overalls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' looks like a noun but is a verb: the words around cover the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Icing a cake is putting a sugar coating on top, a way of adorning it.

clue.text: Try and keep quiet and gracious

parts.note: to have a go is to try
sh is the call to keep quiet

explanation.surface: Advice to attempt silence and good manners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gracious' is the exclamation as in 'Goodness gracious!', not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are mild exclamations of surprise, so one stands in for the other.

clue.text: Cool cryptic setter meeting King Edward

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: CR is Carolus Rex, Latin for King Charles
Ed is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter meets royalty and seems trendy.
explanation.walkthrough: CR stands for Carolus Rex, Latin for King Charles, a common crossword king.
explanation.definitionFit: Street cred is credibility among fashionable young people, so having it is being fashionable.
